<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />probably a particular tree is meant); 19:9, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}} ({{GHGheb|text=הָֽעַלְמָה}}, i.e. ''the'' particular ''maiden'', through whom the prophet’s announcement shall be fulfilled; we should say ''a maiden'' [cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=8|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13|hidebook=1}}]; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=9|verse=31}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|s}}
So always ''to write in the book'' (or ''on the scroll'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=10}}), i.e. not in ''the'' book already in use, but in the book which is to be devoted to that purpose, equivalent to ''in a book, on a scroll'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=17|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=23}}. Especially instructive for this use of the article is the phrase {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם}}, which does not simply refer back to the previous narrative in the sense of ''the same day'', but is used exactly like our ''one day'' (properly meaning on the particular day when it happened, i.e. ''on a certain day''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=6}}, 13. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=11}} even {{GHGheb|text=כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|t}}
The article is sometimes used in this way before collectives in the singular, which are not meant to denote (like the examples given under ''l'') a whole class, but only that part of it which applies to the given case; thus {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֹרֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַיּוֹנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=8|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=הַצִּרְעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=23|verse=28}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|u}}
'''5.''' When a substantive is defined by the article, or by a suffix, or by a following genitive determinate in any way (see the examples below), the attribute belonging to it (whether adjective, participle, ordinal, or demonstrative pronoun) necessarily takes the article (see, however, the Rem.), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=10|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=הָעִיר הַגְּדֹלָה|translate=the great city}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=יָֽדְךָ הַֽחֲזָקָה|translate=thy strong hand}}. A genitive following the substantive may, according to {{GHGpar|127|a}}, be determined either by the article, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ הַבְּלִיַּעַל הַזֶּה|translate=this worthless man}} (prop. ''man of worthlessness''; cf. also such examples as {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=36|verse=18}}, where the article is prefixed only to a second genitive following the noun); or as a proper name, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=11|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=מַֽעֲשֵׂה יְהֹוָה הַגָּדֹל|translate=the great work of the Lord}}; or by a suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=עַבְדֵי אֲדֹנִי הַקְּטַנִּים}} ''the least of my master’s servants''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|v}}
When several attributes (whether connected by {{GHGterm|Wāw}} or not) follow a determinate substantive, each of them takes the article, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=10|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=הָאֵל הַגָּדֹל הַגִּבֹּר וְהַנּוֹרָא|translate=the great God, the mighty, and the terrible}}. Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=19}}, in both of which places a demonstrative with the article also follows the adjective.<ref>The demonstrative used adjectivally is generally placed ''after'' the adjective proper; in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=עַמְּךָ הַזֶּה הַגָּדוֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=1|verse=10}} the adjective forms a further (fresh) addition to {{GHGheb|text=עַמְּךָ הַזֶּה}}.</ref>

Rem. 1. The article is, however, not infrequently used also—

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|w}}
(''a'') With the attribute alone, when it is added to an originally indefinite substantive as a subsequent limitation; so always with ordinal numbers after {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}},<ref>Cf. Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, 3rd ed., § 209; M. Lambert, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 31, 279 f.—The omission of the article from the substantive is not to be regarded in ''this'' instance as an indication of late style, and consequently cannot be put forward as a proof of the late origin of the ‘Priestly Code’ (cf. Dillmann on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=31}}, Holzinger, ''Einl. in d. Hexateuch'', p. 465, and especially Driver in the {{GHGcite|title=Journal of Philology}}, xi. 229 f., against Giesebrecht in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZAW.|Zeitschrift für die alttestamentliche Wissenschaft, ed. by B. Stade, Giessen, 1881 ff., and since 1907 by K. Marti.}}}} 1881, p. 265 f.). On the other hand, the common omission of the article from the substantive before a determinate adjective (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כְּנֵ֫סֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה|translate=the great synagogue}}, in the Mishna; cf. Segal, ''Mišnaic Hebrew'', p. 19 ff.) is certainly a later idiom.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=31}} (cf. 2:3, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=10}}, &c.) {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי|translate=the sixth day}} (prop. ''a day'' namely<section end=par126 /><noinclude>
